agent_audits.name: version_check
agent_audits.notes: Read the complete package inventory, both manifests and all four source modules including tests. No dependencies, unsafe code, native code or own build script. The sole production ambient authority is launching the caller-selected RUSTC (or rustc on PATH) with fixed --verbose --version arguments using Command without a shell, and reading compiler feature environment flags. This is appropriate for a build-time compiler probe, under the same trusted-toolchain assumption as Cargo; child output is not bounded and no timeout is imposed, so this is not an API for executing attacker-selected compilers. Version and date parsing use checked u16 parsing, fixed arrays and early return before a fourth element can be stored; packed shifts have fixed valid widths. String iteration is finite and UTF-8 safe. Dates reject out-of-range month/day but are not calendar validation (e.g. February 31); channel recognition intentionally accepts suffix matches. Those are compiler metadata helpers, not authorization/date validation. Feature flags only affect the caller build configuration, never execute model/import text or select a network destination. Tests read optional excluded static fixtures only when present. No serious production exploit identified in reasonable build-time use. This is a new safe-to-deploy review, not an upgrade of the fuzz safe-to-run audit.

agent_audits.name: stable_deref_trait
agent_audits.notes: Read the entire single-module crate including unsafe marker contracts, every unsafe impl, documentation examples, both manifests and archive inventory. No dependencies, build script, raw pointer operations, native code or ambient I/O. Reasoned about each unsafe impl: Box/Vec/String and owned path/C/OS strings dereference to separately allocated storage stable across moves; their shared methods cannot reallocate the target. The concrete Cow str/slice/path/CStr/OsStr forms preserve target address through shared access; ownership conversion requires mutable access outside the StableDeref promise. Rc/Arc keep target allocation fixed and are the owned types allowed CloneStableDeref; mutable access uses normal unique-borrow rules, not a blanket CloneStableDeref on mutable references. Ref/RefMut and lock guards hold the borrow/lock while dereferencing to the same target. Shared and mutable references preserve pointee location; CloneStableDeref is implemented only for shared references. Arc impls are gated on pointer atomics. The unsafe traits explicitly bind downstream implementers; this review does not certify external unsafe implementations or consumers that violate aliasing/lifetimes or retain references after a guard drops. All std, alloc and no-default configurations were considered.
